content.text: The cardiovascular and respiratory systems are intimately linked to meet tissue oxygen demands. During exercise, both cardiac output and ventilation increase. The V/Q ratio (ventilation-perfusion ratio) ensures matching of air and blood flow. Shunting occurs when ventilation and perfusion are mismatched. Pulmonary hypertension results from increased pulmonary vascular resistance. The cardiopulmonary response to exercise involves: Increased heart rate, Increased stroke volume, Increased tidal volume and respiratory rate, Increased cardiac output, Oxygen extraction by tissues increases.

content.text: The respiratory system regulates acid-base balance through CO2 elimination. Increased ventilation (hyperventilation) eliminates CO2, reducing H+ (respiratory alkalosis). Decreased ventilation (hypoventilation) retains CO2, increasing H+ (respiratory acidosis). The renal system compensates by adjusting bicarbonate reabsorption. The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation relates pH, bicarbonate, and PCO2. Buffers include bicarbonate, phosphate, and proteins. Compensation mechanisms restore pH toward normal.

content.text: Common cardiopulmonary disorders include: Hypertension (chronic high BP), Coronary artery disease (atherosclerosis, angina, MI), Heart failure (reduced cardiac output), Arrhythmias (irregular rhythm), COPD (chronic bronchitis, emphysema), Asthma (airway hyperreactivity), Pulmonary embolism (blockage of pulmonary artery), Pneumonia (lung infection), Hypoxia (low tissue O2), Cyanosis (bluish discoloration due to low O2). Diagnostic tests include ECG, echocardiography, spirometry, pulse oximetry, arterial blood gases (ABGs).
